title: Content Calendar, Plus a Project Home You Can Customize
summary: See scheduled content on a calendar, drag to reschedule, and arrange project home with a Customize menu. Plus: only the latest schedule runs.
body_markdown:
You can now see what is going out, and when, without opening Objects one at a time. This update adds a content calendar to every Bucket, brings the next seven days to project home, and lets each member arrange project home the way they work.


## Content calendar


Go to **Bucket > Calendar** to see your content by date.


- **Three kinds of events.** Drafts scheduled to publish are blue, Objects scheduled to unpublish are orange, and Objects already published are gray.
- **Month and Agenda views.** Month shows the whole grid. Agenda lists events by day and marks the current time.
- **Drag to reschedule.** Drag a scheduled event to another day. The time of day stays the same, and past days can't be selected.
- **Filter by Object type.** The calendar remembers your selection for each Bucket.
- **Open any event** to go straight to the Object.


Dates are shown in your browser's timezone. Contributors see only the Objects they created, in the Object types they can access. See the[calendar docs](https://www.cosmicjs.com/docs/dashboard/buckets#calendar) .


## A simpler project home


- **Coming up.** Project home shows what publishes or unpublishes in the next seven days, with a link to the full calendar.
- **Customize.** Select **Customize** to drag sections into a new order or hide the ones you don't use. Your layout is saved to your account for each project, so it follows you across devices and doesn't change what teammates see. **Reset to default** brings back the default order for your role.
- **Less to scroll past.** Project totals now sit on one line under the project name, Buckets are compact cards at the bottom, and Insights shows a one-line prompt until you set it up.


See the[project home docs](https://www.cosmicjs.com/docs/dashboard/projects#project-home) .


## Only the latest schedule runs


Before this update, changing an Object's publish date, or publishing it by hand, could leave the old date on an earlier revision. When that date arrived, the older content could be published over your newer changes. Now, saving a new schedule or publishing cancels the schedule on older revisions, so only the latest one runs.


## Get Started


- Open any Bucket and select **Calendar** in the sidebar.
- Open a project and select **Customize** to arrange project home.
